lesson.title: Real or Scam? The Surprise Text

character.name: Biscuit
character.description: A golden retriever who trusts everyone. Once almost paid a fake toll. Has never been in a car.

intro.speech: I owe $4.15 in tolls?? I don't even drive. Should I just pay it to be safe?

messages.text: Help!! I got this text. Do I have to pay it?

forwarded.text: You have an unpaid toll balance of $4.15. Pay by today to avoid a $50 late fee: fastrak-tollpay.com

messages.text: Stop! Don't tap that link. That's a scam text.
It's a text from someone pretending to be a company you trust. They want your money or your secret codes.
In 2024, people told the government they lost $470 million to scam texts!
messages.source: FTC Data Spotlight, April 2025: "In 2024, people reported $470 million in losses to these scams." https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/data-visualizations/data-spotlight/2025/04/top-text-scams-2024

messages.text: $470 million?! That's a LOT of dog treats.
Scam texts can look really real. But they leave clues, and you can learn to spot them.

outro.title: Lesson complete!
outro.speech: You saved me $4.15 AND my dignity. Same time tomorrow?
outro.rule: Surprise text + a problem + a rush + an ask = stop. Open the real app yourself.

signs.pretend: Pretend: claims to be someone you trust
signs.problem: Problem: says something is wrong (or you won a prize)
signs.pressure: Pressure: rushes you so you don't stop and think
signs.pay: Pay a weird way: gift cards, crypto, wire, a link

pronunciations.dmv-ca-notice.info: D M V dash C A dash notice dot info

message.text: You have an unpaid toll balance of $4.15. Pay by today to avoid a $50 late fee: fastrak-tollpay.com

correct.text: You caught it! I was SO close to tapping that.

incorrect.text: That's a scam. Toll agencies don't text surprise fines with a payment link. Notice the deadline: today.

questions.prompt: Tap the part that's trying to rush you.

segments.text: You have an unpaid toll balance of $4.15.
Pay by today to avoid a $50 late fee

newWord.definition: A tight deadline or scary consequence meant to rush you.

correct.text: Pressure! A tight deadline plus a scary fee. Scammers rush you so you don't stop and think.

incorrect.text: Pressure is the deadline: "Pay by today to avoid a $50 late fee." It's there to rush you.

pairs.hint: Claims to be someone you trust
Real companies don't ask for this

correct.text: Those are the 4 signs of a scam: Pretend, Problem, Pressure, Pay a weird way.

incorrect.text: Close! Tap a sign's label to see its hint, then try the pair again.

questions.prompt: Biscuit ordered a chew toy yesterday. Then this arrives. Real or scam?

message.text: Your package is out for delivery today. No action needed.

correct.text: Nice. It asks for nothing: no link, no money, no rush.

incorrect.text: Good instinct to check! This one asks for nothing. If you're ever unsure, opening the USPS app yourself is safe either way.

message.text: We blocked a suspicious $892 charge. To unlock your account, reply with the 6-digit code we just sent you.

options.feedback: WAIT. A real bank never asks you to read back a code. That code is the key to your account.
Asking for it again still plays along. The bank should never need that code from you.

options.text: I'll call the number on my card instead.

correct.text: Exactly. Call the number on your card, not one from the text.

incorrect.text: WAIT. A real bank never asks you to read back a code. That code is the key to your account.

correct.text: Never share a one-time code with anyone who texts you. Write it on my food bowl.

incorrect.text: Correct rule: "Never share a one-time code with anyone who texts you."

message.text: Your package can't be delivered. Update your address: usps-redelivery.net

options.label: Tap the link and update his address
options.feedback: That link goes to the scammer, not USPS.

options.label: Reply "STOP"
options.feedback: Replying tells scammers your number is real. Don't reply at all.

options.label: Close the text and check the USPS app himself

correct.text: The safe move: skip the link and open the real app yourself.

incorrect.text: The safe move is to close the text and check the USPS app yourself.

questions.prompt: Biscuit spotted a scam text. What's the best next move?

options.text: Forward it to 7726 (SPAM), then delete it

options.feedback: Any reply tells the scammer your number works.

options.text: Ignore it but keep it forever
options.feedback: Reporting helps your carrier block the scammer for everyone.

correct.text: 7726 spells SPAM on your keypad. Your carrier uses these reports to block scammers.

incorrect.text: Forward it to 7726 (SPAM), then delete it. Carriers use reports to block scammers.

questions.prompt: Scam detective! Tap ALL the signs in this text.

segments.text: Your driver's license will be suspended

correct.text: This one had ALL FOUR. Also, again, I am a dog. I do not have a license.

incorrect.text: All four signs are here: Pretend (DMV), Problem (suspended license), Pressure (today), Pay a weird way (gift card).

q10.rule: If the learner missed any question in q1-q9, Q10 is the replay for the concept of the FIRST missed question. If they missed nothing, Q10 is the boss question.

pressure.prompt: Replay! Tap the part that's trying to rush you.

segments.text: You have an unpaid parking citation.
Pay within 2 hours or your car will be towed

correct.text: You got it this time! "Within 2 hours" plus a scary threat = Pressure.

incorrect.text: The rush is "Pay within 2 hours or your car will be towed." That's Pressure.

pairs.hint: Claims to be someone you trust
Real companies don't ask for this

incorrect.text: Pretend, Problem, Pressure, Pay a weird way. You'll see them everywhere now.

legit.prompt: Replay! Biscuit just booked a vet appointment. Real or scam?

message.text: Reminder: Biscuit's checkup is Tuesday at 3:00 PM. See you then!

correct.text: Real! It matches something Biscuit did, and it asks for nothing.

incorrect.text: This one's real: it matches his calendar and asks for nothing. Not every text is a scam.

message.text: Hey! I accidentally sent my verification code to your phone. Can you text it back to me?

options.feedback: That code is for YOUR account. Sending it lets them in.

options.text: Which code? I got a few
options.feedback: Still playing along. Don't share any code.

correct.text: Never share a one-time code, even with someone who sounds nice.

incorrect.text: Never share a one-time code with anyone who texts you. That code unlocks YOUR account.

message.text: Your card has been frozen. Unfreeze it here: goldenbank-unlock.co

options.label: Tap the link to unfreeze
options.feedback: That link goes to the scammer.

options.label: Open the Golden Bank app himself
Reply "is this real?"
options.feedback: The scammer will just say yes.

correct.text: Open the real app yourself. Works every time, real or fake.

incorrect.text: The safe move is opening the bank's app yourself.

report.prompt: Replay! What number do you forward scam texts to?

options.feedback: 911 is for emergencies. Scam texts go to 7726.

incorrect.text: Forward scam texts to 7726 (SPAM), then delete them.

boss.prompt: Boss question! This text has perfect grammar and sounds professional. Real or scam?

message.text: We noticed unusual sign-in activity on your account. For your security, please verify your identity using the secure link below. Thank you for banking with us. goldenbank-verify.com

correct.text: Scammers use AI now, so no typos doesn't mean safe. It's still a surprise problem plus a link.

incorrect.text: Scam. Perfect grammar doesn't mean safe; scammers use AI now. It's still a surprise problem plus a link. Open your bank's app yourself.
